scope: Pinned SSH synchronization of complete Sharpa visual and collision meshes to the A800 host
summary: An authenticated sparse SSH checkout reached the exact official revision but blob transfer was stopped after sustained low throughput; the partial checkout was not used by inference and no trajectory result is claimed.
evidence: GitHub SSH authentication and remote HEAD 6eea427eb24189519f32b9f21674cd534d3f973c were verified through agent forwarding.
The remote partial clone recorded the exact revision but had not materialized wave_01 files; its fetch pack reached only 6.6 MiB after more than three minutes.
All related local and remote transfer processes were terminated before handoff; the incomplete checkout was never selected as an exact asset.
lessons: Source-revision verification and full asset materialization are separate preflight gates.
A correct Git commit cannot substitute for verifying every mesh required by the MJCF on the execution host.
limitations: The A800 host still lacks a complete pinned left Sharpa mesh checkout for the full-q render experiment.
No robot trajectory or performance measurement was produced.
next_actions: Stage the complete hashed asset bundle through the normal artifact cache, then resume the full-q run in a fresh experiment directory.
